problem:
If $\,T\,$ is a linear transformation and $\,T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11\end{aligned}]$, then find $T([\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]).$

| $\,T([\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 10\end{aligned}])=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation, it must satisfy $T(kv)=kT(v).$ Noting that $[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]=2[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]) & =T(2[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =2T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -22\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
